sandhi.note: Final m before a consonant becomes anusvāra.

samasa.vigraha: सृष्टिः च स्थितिः च विनाशः च सृष्टिस्थितिविनाशाः, तेषाम्
samasa.sense: of the three acts of the world: its making, its keeping and its ending
samasa.alt: The compound takes the gender of its last member (विनाश, m.) and the plural for three members.

samasa.type: karmadhāraya (भूत ‘being, existing as’, as in आधारभूता, 11.4)
samasa.sense: you who are the very power behind creation, preservation and dissolution

samasa.vigraha: गुणानाम् आश्रयः यस्यां सा गुणाश्रया, तत्सम्बुद्धौ
samasa.literal: she in whom the guṇas have their resting-place
samasa.sense: the ground on which the three guṇas — sattva, rajas, tamas — rest
samasa.alt: Often translated as a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa, गुणानाम् आश्रयः ‘support of the guṇas’; but a tatpuruṣa keeps the gender of आश्रय (m.), and the feminine vocative -आश्रये shows the bahuvrīhi. The meaning is the same.

morph.note: -मय (mayaṭ) means ‘made of, consisting of’; its feminine is -मयी (vocative -मये). गुणाश्रये and गुणमये together say that she both supports the guṇas and is made of them.
सनातन ‘eternal’ (from सना ‘always’) with feminine -ī; vocative with the ī shortened.
Genitive plural of an a-stem dvandva: -आनाम्. It depends on the first member of the next word (शक्ति-), a construction common in verse.

mantras.anvaya: (हे) सृष्टिस्थितिविनाशानां शक्तिभूते सनातनि गुणाश्रये गुणमये नारायणि, ते नमः अस्तु।
mantras.anvaya_en: Vocatives (शक्तिभूते, सनातनि, गुणाश्रये, गुणमये, नारायणि) followed by the refrain; the genitive dvandva depends on शक्ति-.
mantras.lit: O you who are the power of creation, preservation and destruction, O eternal one, O resting-place of the guṇas, O you who consist of the guṇas, O Nārāyaṇī, homage be to you.
mantras.tr: Eternal one, you are the power that creates, sustains and destroys; the guṇas rest in you and are made of you: O Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you.
mantras.tr_note: The vocative epithets are turned into statements. ‘Are made of you’ renders गुणमये (‘consisting of the guṇas’) from the other side; a closer rendering is ‘you are made of the guṇas’.

comm.t: The Goddess is the single power behind the three acts of the world — creation, continuance and destruction — and the eternal ground of the three guṇas, which both rest in her and make up her form.

The verse gathers the teaching of Brahmā’s hymn: in creation she is creation, in preserving she is preservation, at the end she is dissolution (1.76–77), and she is the prakṛti that brings forth the three guṇas (1.78, गुणत्रयविभाविनी). The tradition links the three acts with the three guṇas (rajas, sattva, tamas) and with Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Rudra, all of whom act through her power. The word सनातनी returns in 12.39.

Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) has सृष्टिकर्त्री (264), संहारिणी (268), त्रिगुणात्मिका (763) and also गुणातीता (961), ‘beyond the guṇas’. The two texts are separate works; together the names show the Śākta view that she is both within and beyond the guṇas.

sandhi.split: शरण + आगत + दीन + आर्त + परित्राण + पर + अयने
sandhi.type: vowel sandhi inside a compound (savarṇa-dīrgha, three times)
sandhi.note: a + ā → ā (शरणागत, दीनार्त) and a + a → ā (परायण). The n of अयन becomes ṇ after the r of पर (परायण), by the rule of retroflexion inside a word.

samasa.vigraha: शरणम् आगताः शरणागताः; दीनाः च ते आर्ताः च दीनार्ताः; शरणागताः दीनार्ताः शरणागतदीनार्ताः; तेषां परित्राणम्; तत् परम् अयनं यस्याः सा शरणागतदीनार्तपरित्राणपरायणा, तत्सम्बुद्धौ
samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (-परायण ‘having … as highest goal’), containing a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa (…परित्राण), a karmadhāraya (शरणागतदीनार्त), a dvitīyā tatpuruṣa (शरणागत) and a dvandva or karmadhāraya (दीनार्त)
samasa.literal: she whose highest aim is the rescue of the wretched and afflicted who have come for refuge
samasa.sense: she who lives to save the helpless who turn to her
samasa.alt: शरणागतदीनार्त can also be a three-member dvandva, ‘those who have taken refuge, the wretched and the afflicted’ (three groups instead of one). The karmadhāraya, one group described three ways, is the more common reading; the sense differs little.

samasa.sense: as in 11.3 (प्रपन्नार्तिहरे); the genitive सर्वस्य outside the compound depends on its first member आर्ति

morph.note: A single compound fills the whole first line (eight syllables). परायण at the end of a compound means ‘wholly devoted to, intent on’ (lit. ‘having … as the highest resort’). परित्राण is the action noun of परि + √त्रै ‘to rescue’.
-हर is the agent of √हृ ‘to take away’ in compounds, feminine -हरा; vocative -हरे.

mantras.anvaya: (हे) शरणागतदीनार्तपरित्राणपरायणे, सर्वस्य आर्तिहरे देवि नारायणि, ते नमः अस्तु।
mantras.anvaya_en: Two vocative phrases and the refrain; the first line is a single compound.
mantras.lit: O you who are wholly intent on rescuing the wretched and afflicted who have come for refuge, O Goddess who take away the distress of all, O Nārāyaṇī, homage be to you.
mantras.tr: You live to rescue the helpless and suffering who come to you for shelter, and you take away the sorrow of all: O Goddess Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you.
mantras.tr_note: The vocatives are turned into statements; ‘live to rescue’ renders -परायणे, ‘wholly intent on’.

comm.t: The Goddess is greeted as the one whose whole purpose is to rescue those who come to her in helplessness and pain, and who takes away the distress of all.

The verse returns to the first word of the hymn: प्रपन्नार्तिहरे (11.3) becomes सर्वस्यार्तिहरे, and the prapanna, the one who has come for refuge, becomes the शरणागत. The tradition values the verse as a prayer of surrender: it asks for nothing but names her as the refuge of the helpless.
A modern reading: the verse does not ask the one who comes for refuge to be worthy, only to be in need and to come. Refuge is described from the side of the one who gives it.

sandhi.type: vowel sandhi inside a compound (savarṇa-dīrgha); visarga kept
sandhi.note: a + a → ā (कौशाम्भः). The s-stem अम्भस् shows visarga before the unvoiced k of क्षरिका, kept as printed.

samasa.vigraha: हंसैः युक्तम् हंसयुक्तम्; हंसयुक्तं च तत् विमानं च हंसयुक्तविमानम्; हंसयुक्तविमाने तिष्ठति इति हंसयुक्तविमानस्था, तत्सम्बुद्धौ
samasa.type: upapada tatpuruṣa (-स्थ ‘standing, seated’), containing a karmadhāraya (हंसयुक्तविमान) and a tṛtīyā tatpuruṣa (हंसयुक्त)
samasa.literal: she who stands in the car yoked with swans
samasa.sense: Brahmāṇī, riding the swan-drawn chariot of Brahmā

samasa.vigraha: ब्रह्माण्याः रूपम् ब्रह्माणीरूपम्; तत् धारयति इति ब्रह्माणीरूपधारिणी, तत्सम्बुद्धौ
samasa.type: upapada tatpuruṣa (-धारिन् ‘bearing’) containing a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa
samasa.literal: bearer of the form of Brahmāṇī
samasa.sense: you who take the form of Brahmā’s Śakti

samasa.vigraha: कौशम् अम्भः कौशाम्भः; तत् क्षरयति इति कौशाम्भःक्षरिका, तत्सम्बुद्धौ
samasa.sense: you who sprinkle water consecrated with kuśa grass

morph.note: कौश is a taddhita from कुश (with vṛddhi): ‘of kuśa grass’, i.e. water sprinkled with or sanctified by kuśa. क्षरिका is an agent noun from √क्षर् ‘to flow’ (here ‘to make flow, sprinkle’) with the suffix -aka, feminine -ikā; the formation is uncommon, and the word is known chiefly from this verse.
ब्रह्माणी is the feminine of ब्रह्मन् formed with -ānī (like इन्द्राणी, रुद्राणी): Brahmā’s consort or power. -धारिन् (√धृ with -in) ‘bearing’, feminine -धारिणी.

mantras.anvaya: (हे) हंसयुक्तविमानस्थे ब्रह्माणीरूपधारिणि कौशाम्भःक्षरिके देवि नारायणि, ते नमः अस्तु।
mantras.anvaya_en: Three descriptive vocatives naming Brahmāṇī, then देवि नारायणि and the refrain.
mantras.lit: O you who are seated in the celestial car yoked with swans, who bear the form of Brahmāṇī, who sprinkle water with kuśa grass, O Goddess, O Nārāyaṇī, homage be to you.
mantras.tr: Riding the swan-drawn chariot in the form of Brahmāṇī, sprinkling the water hallowed with kuśa grass: O Goddess Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you.
mantras.tr_note: ‘Hallowed with kuśa’ interprets कौश- (‘of kuśa’): in rites, water is sprinkled with a bunch of kuśa grass.

comm.t: With this verse the hymn turns to the Mātṛkās, the Śaktis of the gods who fought beside the Goddess against Raktabīja’s army (chapter 8): Brahmāṇī here, then Māheśvarī, Kaumārī, Vaiṣṇavī, Vārāhī, Nārasiṃhī, Aindrī, Śivadūtī and Cāmuṇḍā (11.14–21). Each is greeted as a form of the one Nārāyaṇī.

The picture is the one given in the battle: Brahmāṇī came on a car drawn by swans, with rosary and water-pot (8.15), and struck down the asuras by sprinkling water from her kamaṇḍalu (8.33), water made pure by mantra (9.38). The hymn turns her weapon into an image of blessing: the sprinkling of consecrated water.
Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) also has the name ब्रह्माणी (821). The Mātṛkās are a shared Śākta group; the two texts are separate works.

flags.uncertain: क्षरिका is a rare formation (from √क्षर् ‘to flow, let flow’); the sense ‘sprinkler of water’ is clear from the context and from 8.33, but the exact derivation is not certain.

samasa.vigraha: त्रिशूलं च चन्द्रः च अहिः च त्रिशूलचन्द्राहयः; तान् धरति इति त्रिशूलचन्द्राहिधरा, तत्सम्बुद्धौ
samasa.type: upapada tatpuruṣa (-धर ‘bearing’) containing an itaretara dvandva
samasa.literal: bearer of trident, moon and serpent
samasa.sense: you who carry Śiva’s emblems: the trident in hand, the crescent moon on the head, the serpent as ornament

samasa.vigraha: महान् च असौ वृषभः च महावृषभः; महावृषभं वाहयति इति महावृषभवाहिनी, तत्सम्बुद्धौ
samasa.type: upapada tatpuruṣa (-वाहिन्, from the causative of √वह्: ‘one who has (it) carry her, rider’) containing a karmadhāraya (महावृषभ)
samasa.literal: she who rides the great bull
samasa.alt: Also analysed with the possessive suffix -in on वाह ‘mount’: ‘having the great bull as her mount’ (महावृषभः वाहः अस्याः अस्ति). The sense is the same.

samasa.sense: as Māheśvarī, the Śakti of Maheśvara (Śiva)

morph.note: An instrumental, not a vocative: the verse has no vocative ‘O Māheśvarī’ but says ‘(you who are) in the form of Māheśvarī’. The refrain’s नारायणि is the only name in the address.
महत् ‘great’ becomes महा at the head of a karmadhāraya (a rule of compound formation, not of sandhi), as in महासुर (11.2).

mantras.anvaya: (हे) त्रिशूलचन्द्राहिधरे महावृषभवाहिनि, माहेश्वरीस्वरूपेण (स्थिते) नारायणि, ते नमः अस्तु।
mantras.anvaya_en: Two vocatives, an instrumental of manner (with a participle such as स्थिते understood), and the refrain.
mantras.lit: O bearer of the trident, the moon and the serpent, O rider of the great bull, O Nārāyaṇī (who are) in the form of Māheśvarī, homage be to you.
mantras.tr: Bearing the trident, the crescent moon and the serpent, riding the great bull in the form of Māheśvarī: O Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you.
mantras.tr_note: ‘Crescent’ is added to ‘moon’ (चन्द्र), as Māheśvarī is described in 8.16 with the moon’s digit (चन्द्ररेखा).

comm.t: The second of the Mātṛkās: Māheśvarī, Śiva’s Śakti, with his emblems — the trident, the crescent moon and the serpent — and riding his great bull.

So she came to the battle in chapter 8: mounted on the bull, holding the trident, with great serpents for bracelets and the moon’s crescent as her ornament (8.16), and she slew asuras with her trident (8.34, 8.49). The hymn salutes the same figure as a form of Nārāyaṇī.
Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) also has the name माहेश्वरी (208). The two texts are separate works.
